verdict.rationale: Supabase documents branching that creates isolated environments, with preview environments per pull request, for testing database schema changes without affecting production. It also documents version-controlled migration files developed against a local stack. However, the evidence never shows a merge or promote-to-production step, nor any online or non-locking DDL guarantee, so the 'without locking production' part is unproven. Older community comments call migrations a weakness, but they predate branching and do not concretely contradict it. missing for 10: documented merge/promotion of branch schema changes to production, online/non-locking DDL or deploy-request safety checks, independent hands-on corroboration of the branching workflow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can ship schema changes safely — online DDL, deploy requests, or branch-and-merge workflows — without locking or breaking production

citations.quote: You can use these branching environments to create and test changes like new configurations, database schemas, or features without affecting your production setup.
Branching takes this further, adding isolated preview environments for each pull request.
then capture your changes in schema migration files, which can be saved in version control.
